name: Alaïa
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $1750 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's knit and jersey dresses, coats, Le Teckel and Le Coeur bags and fishnet ballet flats (about $1,000), sold through its own boutiques, website and Bergdorf Goodman.
origin: Founded in Paris, France in 1964 by Azzedine Alaïa.

ownership.owner: Compagnie Financière Richemont SA (SIX Swiss Exchange: CFR)

quote.q: Clothes explore the rapport between cloth and skin, between form and function.

opview: “Clothes explore the rapport between cloth and skin, between form and function.” — Alaïa (house), WS27 Collection presentation, maison-alaia.com

craft_evidence.mills: no (Japanese denim named by country on some jeans)
craft_evidence.madein: 96% (76 of 79: Italy 60, France 6, Japan 5, Portugal 4, Madagascar 1)
craft_evidence.heritage: not stated on the pages read (no maison-history page in the US store navigation)
craft_evidence.process: partial — a Homo Faber 2026 page documents a knitted gown with individually cut, hand-sewn silk feathers; the denim page says 'hand-sanded'
craft_evidence.reasoning: Nearly every product page states a country, mostly Italy and some France, and the Homo Faber page documents knitwear savoir-faire on a showpiece gown. No atelier, maker or mill is named for the range sold, and the store carries no house-history page, so it's a 2. I'd expect the record to know more about the Paris atelier than the store shows.
